subject: Invoice submission channel — decision framework & PO exception playbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwave.com>, BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice submission channel — decision framework & PO exception playbook

Hi Elena / BrightWave team,

Following our discovery call last week, I put together a lightweight decision framework to help determine when we require portal submission vs when email (SMTP) ingestion is acceptable. The goal is to minimize friction for vendors while protecting PO matching and ledger integrity. Please review and tell me if anything here would block BrightWave from following the approach.

Proposal (high level):
- Default: portal/webfront for all suppliers who can reasonably onboard (~90%). Portal provides structured CSV/JSON, subject-token idempotency, and automatic PO-match.
- Accept email invoices when one of these is true: vendor is low volume (<5 invoices/month), vendor cannot use the portal for technical or policy reasons, or vendor is under a short-term pilot.
- PO-required rule: if Redwood PO referenced, invoice must include PO number in subject token or invoice body. For PO-less invoices, route to the PO-exception playbook (fast triage + 5-business-day SLA).
- Minimal invoice fields for email ingestion: invoice number, invoice date (ISO), amount, currency, Redwood entity, and line-item csv or PDF attachment. We can accept PDFs but structured data preferred.

Operational notes:
- Email subject conventions: "INV|<supplier-id>|<po-number>|<invoice-number>" when possible to help automated routing. We will accept free-form but subject tokens speed processing.
- Attachments: accept PDF and CSV. PDFs must be readable OCR; recommend attaching a one-line CSV when available.
- Exceptions: we will provide a PO-exception form (single sheet) for suppliers who cannot supply PO numbers; finance will triage and create a short-lived PO or route for manual approval.

Next steps: if this looks good from BrightWave's side we will: 1) share the minimal CSV spec and subject-token examples; 2) send onboarding form + PO-exception worksheet; 3) schedule a 30-minute cutover call for any pilot vendors.

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we commit:

1) For vendors that are "low volume", can BrightWave still ask them to use the portal if they are already portal-enabled? Or is the intent to allow email for any vendor that requests it?
2) If a PDF invoice is attached without the subject token, can Redwood still auto-extract PO number (we have OCR that sometimes finds it) or will it go to manual triage?

I've attached an example invoice PDF from one of our small suppliers — it has a PO on the header but the filename doesn't follow the token pattern.

We can prototype with 10 suppliers next week if that helps.

Best,

Naomi — forwarding notes from my side and a small tweak suggestion.

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 11:02 AM Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwave.com> wrote:
> Hi Naomi,
> 
> Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions before we commit:
> 
> 1) For vendors that are "low volume", can BrightWave still ask them to use the portal if they are already portal-enabled? Or is the intent to allow email for any vendor that requests it?
> 2) If a PDF invoice is attached without the subject token, can Redwood still auto-extract PO number (we have OCR that sometimes finds it) or will it go to manual triage?

My replies inline:
- Low-volume vendors: prefer portal-first if already enabled. The "email allowed" clause is primarily for vendors who cannot reasonably onboard (legacy EDI shops, one-off consultants, or highly regulated vendors). We'll note that in the playbook language.
- OCR: our pipeline tries to auto-extract PO numbers from PDFs; success rate depends on template. If OCR yields a high-confidence match, we attempt auto-match; if confidence is low or ambiguous, it drops to the PO-exception flow. We should include confidence thresholds in the Ops doc (e.g., >85% auto-match).

Action items for Ops/Onboarding: 
- Naomi: share the PO-exception single-sheet (template) and the CSV spec for portal ingestion.
- Marissa: add an entry in onboarding tracker for a 10-vendor pilot and collect sample invoices.
- Jordan: I'll draft the confidence thresholds and a short triage play for finance.

Jordan
Enterprise Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Elena / team — thanks for the quick replies. Summary and next steps below.

Summary decisions (agreed):
- Portal remains our preferred default for all portal-capable vendors. BrightWave should encourage portal use when available.
- Email ingestion allowed as an exception: low-volume or inability to onboard. We'll document this as "email backstop" rather than a full alternative.
- OCR auto-extract allowed: Redwood will attempt auto-extraction and auto-match at confidence >= 85%. Anything below that goes to the PO-exception triage.

Attached I'm sharing: 1) PO-exception single-sheet (fill-once per invoice series); 2) minimal CSV spec and 3) sample subject-token examples. We've also added a short triage SLA: 5 business days for PO-exception acknowledgement, 12 business days to resolution unless expedited.

Pilot: Naomi to Marissa: please create onboarding tracker entry for BrightWave pilot (10 suppliers) and collect the PDFs Elena will share. Marissa, please confirm the pilot start date (suggest Monday 2026-06-21).

Elena: please confirm who at BrightWave will be the point-of-contact for supplier communications (name + email). Once we have that I'll send the Drive link with onboarding artifacts and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.

Thanks,
Naomi
